nodes.name: Dune grasses
nodes.desc: Tussock grasses that grow on Namib dunes and gravel plains and feed grazers, seed eaters and termites.

nodes.name: Nara melon
nodes.desc: A spiny, leafless melon plant of coastal dunes that fruits for animals and people. Its roots tap deep water.

nodes.name: Welwitschia
nodes.desc: A long-lived plant with two strap-like leaves. It takes up moisture from fog as well as from groundwater.

nodes.name: Ana tree & riverbed shrubs
nodes.desc: Trees and shrubs along dry rivers. Desert elephants feed on the leaves and seedpods of ana trees in the dry season.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae in the cold, productive Benguela Current, the base of the offshore food chain.

nodes.name: Fog-basking beetles
nodes.desc: Darkling beetles that harvest fog on their bumpy backs and drink the droplets that roll to their mouths. They scavenge wind-blown plant debris.

nodes.name: Sand-diving lizard
nodes.desc: A dune lizard that dives into sand to escape heat and enemies. It eats wind-blown seeds and insects and is itself prey for snakes.

nodes.name: Harvester termites
nodes.desc: Termites that gather dry grass and carry it underground, turning scarce plant matter into food for other animals.

nodes.name: Springbok
nodes.desc: A small antelope of arid plains that grazes and browses and needs little free water.

nodes.name: Gemsbok (oryx)
nodes.desc: A desert antelope that can meet its water needs from wild melons and cucumbers. Lions and hyenas are its natural predators in Africa.

nodes.name: Common ostrich
nodes.desc: A huge flightless bird that eats plants, seeds and some insects on open desert plains.

nodes.name: Desert-adapted elephant
nodes.desc: Elephants that follow dry riverbeds and may walk up to 70 km at night between water points. They eat browse such as ana tree leaves and pods.

nodes.name: Cape anchovy & sardine
nodes.desc: Small schooling fish that eat plankton and feed the seals and seabirds of the Skeleton Coast.

nodes.name: Web-footed gecko
nodes.desc: A night-active dune gecko with webbed feet. It eats small arthropods and gets most of its water from dew on plants.

nodes.name: Namib golden mole
nodes.desc: A blind, sand-swimming mole that hunts insects under the dunes.

nodes.name: Peringuey's adder
nodes.desc: A small sidewinding viper that buries itself in sand and ambushes lizards. Dune lizards with high water content help it get water.

nodes.name: Aardwolf
nodes.desc: A small hyena relative that specializes in eating termites.

nodes.name: Black-backed jackal
nodes.desc: A scavenging hunter of the coast and desert. On the Skeleton Coast it takes seal pups and carrion and even licks moisture from stones.

nodes.name: Brown hyena
nodes.desc: Mostly a scavenger that lives near seal colonies on the Namib coast. It eats seal pups and often steals kills from jackals.

nodes.name: Cape fur seal
nodes.desc: Large colonies breed on the Namib coast and feed on fish at sea. Their pups and carcasses feed jackals, hyenas and lions on land.

nodes.name: Lion
nodes.desc: Lions on the Skeleton Coast prey on seals and shorebirds. Inland they also hunt oryx and springbok.

nodes.name: Coastal fog
nodes.desc: Cold Benguela Current air makes thick fog for much of the year. Plants and beetles drink from it where almost no rain falls.

nodes.name: Wind-blown plant debris
nodes.desc: Dry plant matter carried by wind from the interior feeds dune invertebrates, which in turn support reptiles.

nodes.name: Ephemeral river water
nodes.desc: Dry rivers carry flood pulses and keep groundwater close to the surface, supporting trees, Welwitschia and elephants.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the sand.
